answer: Six-member insurance pools stake 50 each; if one member is proven fake, the pool loses all 300, so members vet newcomers. Admission at a jetty checkpoint needs three of five members to sign a bridge bond tying their own 50 to the newcomer, posted on the public ledger. The kth fake still pays 200, 50 plus 50 per approver, approvals never transfer, so 1,000 fakes cost 200,000. A whisper ring fails: approvals are public, so approvers whose newcomers are proven fake lose their 50 with the pool. An honest identity stakes 50 once, kept after clean epochs.
